# Expert faceplate
Press [bold]VIEW[/bold] at the top of the radio panel until it reads [bold]117G PANEL[/bold].
You are now looking at the radio itself: connectors down the left, the display in the middle, the function switch on the right, soft keys below the glass, and the keypad along the bottom.
This controls the same radio as the [textlink="guided panel" link="AU14CommsANPRCGuided"], but gives you access to settings the guided interface normally leaves on AUTO. It also unlocks several [bold]operator techniques[/bold] that are only available from the faceplate.
It looks more complicated than it is.
Most of the radio is operated with five controls. Learn [bold]Working the glass[/bold], then run through the [bold]drill[/bold] at the end of this page on a live set.
## Working the glass
Almost everything happens through the display.
Each screen is a list of lines. Move the cursor to the line you want, then operate it.
[bold]Key[/bold] [bold]What it does[/bold]
[bold]+ PRE / - PRE[/bold] Move the cursor up and down. The cursor skips lines that cannot be used.
[bold]ENT[/bold] Use the selected line: change a setting, open a page, or confirm an action.
[bold]CLR[/bold] Go back one screen. While typing, delete one character.
[bold]+ PG / - PG[/bold] Move between the main pages.
Soft keys Jump directly to PGM, SEC, SRCH, LOG, OPT, or the ? key card.
[bold]Bright[/bold] lines are settings or actions you can use. Headings divide the screen into sections. Dim text is informational and will not take the cursor.
A lit setting is currently enabled.
Dangerous actions such as zeroizing a fill, destroying a card, starting a recrypto, or pushing a key over the air require confirmation. The first press of ENT [bold]arms[/bold] the action; the second performs it.
If you leave it alone for a few seconds, it disarms automatically.
## The keypad
When you are not entering text or numbers, the number keys act as shortcuts.
[bold]Key[/bold] [bold]Function[/bold]
1 CALL Send a radio check on the working net.
2 LT Cycle the backlight between night, day, and off.
3 MODE Cycle the waveform.
4 SQL Cycle the squelch setting.
5 ZERO Open SEC with the wipe already armed.
6 PWR Switch the radio on or off.
7 8 9 0 Open OPT, PGM, SEC, and LOG.
### Typing
Some settings need you to enter a value directly, such as a frequency, memory label, or station callsign.
When that happens, the keypad switches into input mode. The prompt appears at the bottom of the display.
Press [bold]ENT[/bold] to accept what you entered. Press [bold]CLR[/bold] on an empty field to cancel.
- [bold]Frequencies[/bold] use the [bold]___.___[/bold] format. Enter the megahertz first. Any untouched digit is treated as zero. You must enter at least three digits. - [bold]Text[/bold] uses the letters printed above each number key, like an old telephone keypad. Press 2 once for D, twice for E, three times for F. [bold]0[/bold] enters a space, then a dash. CLR deletes the last character.
## The function switch
The large rotary switch on the right controls the radio's basic operating state.
- [bold]OFF[/bold] - switches the radio off. - [bold]CT[/bold] - switches the radio on in secure operation. Turning to CT again cycles through FH, SC, and CT. - [bold]PT[/bold] - switches to plain-text transmission. Anyone capable of receiving the traffic can read it. - [bold]LD[/bold] - opens the fill page. This position is [bold]sprung[/bold] and returns automatically. - [bold]Z[/bold] - arms the wipe function. Confirm with ENT. This position is also sprung.
LD and Z return to the switch's previous position after use. They do not change your waveform.
That is intentional.
## The readout
The top section of the display remains visible regardless of which page you are using.
- [bold]RX / TX[/bold] - lights when the radio is receiving or transmitting. - [bold]SEC[/bold], [bold]UNSEC[/bold], or [bold]CLEAR[/bold] - shows the current encryption state. - [bold]SIG[/bold] - shows the link quality of your working net. A direct frequency shows [bold]--DIR--[/bold] instead because there is no relay behind it. - [bold]BAT[/bold] - shows the power cell in four bars. - The current memory, frequency, net name, and band, such as [bold]UHF LOS[/bold]. - The settings line - waveform, [bold]SQL[/bold], [bold]PWR[/bold], plus flags for active features: [bold]MON SCAN BURST PS PRI EMCON RXMT[/bold]. - [bold]STN[/bold] - the callsign the radio is transmitting under. - [bold]BIT[/bold] - the radio's self-test. Normally [bold]PASS[/bold]; otherwise it shows the first problem it finds, such as NO CELL, OFF, STOWED, SRCH, or NO NET.
## PGM - net memory
This is the page the faceplate opens on.
- [bold]LOAD STD NETS[/bold] performs the same automatic setup as the guided panel. It only appears when one or more standard nets are missing. - Each memory appears as its own line. A [bold]*[/bold] marks the current working memory. - Press ENT on a memory to open its options: - [bold]WORK THIS NET[/bold] - make this your working net. - [bold]TUNE TO A NET[/bold] - choose from your side's known nets or any resolved enemy net marked INT. - [bold]KEY A FREQUENCY[/bold] - enter a frequency manually. If it matches a known net, that net is loaded. Otherwise it becomes a [bold]direct frequency[/bold]: unrelayed, unencrypted, and only usable by radios or tuned headsets on the same number. - [bold]EMPTY THE MEMORY[/bold] - clear what the memory contains. - [bold]DELETE THE MEMORY[/bold] - remove the memory. - [bold]RENAME[/bold] - change its label. - [bold]ADD NET[/bold] creates another memory and asks you to enter its label.
Direct frequencies must fall within either the 1.000-2.999 MHz military band or the 30.000+ MHz colony softwave band.
## SEC - COMSEC
The SEC page handles encryption and fill cards.
- [bold]SWITCH[/bold] - shows where the physical function switch is currently resting. - [bold]FILL[/bold] - shows the loaded fill card. - [bold]ISSUED TO[/bold] - shows which side owns that fill. - [bold]TRAFFIC[/bold] - shows whether your transmissions are currently encrypted. - [bold]ZEROIZE[/bold] - ejects the fill card. - [bold]DESTROY[/bold] - destroys the loaded card. - [bold]RECRYPTO[/bold] - supersedes every fill card held by your side. Requires command authority. - [bold]SEND KEY OTA[/bold] - sends the current key over the air. See [bold]Over-the-air rekey[/bold].
ZEROIZE, DESTROY, RECRYPTO, and SEND KEY OTA all require the usual arm-and-confirm sequence.
## SRCH - the search receiver
The search receiver hunts for enemy radio traffic across the band.
- [bold]START SEARCH[/bold] begins sweeping for active transmissions. - While searching, the radio is [bold]off every loaded net[/bold], [bold]cannot transmit[/bold], and consumes additional battery. - [bold]HEAD[/bold] shows where the receiver is currently listening. - [bold]CONTACTS[/bold] lists signals the search has found. - [bold]JAMMER DF[/bold] provides tools for locating an active jammer.
Contacts resolve gradually.
A newly detected signal may first appear as something like [bold]2XX.XXX[/bold], then [bold]25X.XXX[/bold], then [bold]259.XXX[/bold], before finally resolving into its exact frequency and net name.
Busy nets resolve more quickly. Partial contacts begin to fade if the signal stops transmitting.
Press ENT on a [bold]resolved[/bold] contact to tune it into your working memory.
Press ENT on a [bold]partial[/bold] contact to park the receiver on it. See [bold]Dwell[/bold] below.
## LOG
The LOG page displays recorded radio traffic.
[bold]NET FILTER[/bold] cycles through nets represented in the log.
[bold]INTERCEPTS ONLY[/bold] hides friendly traffic and leaves only intercepted transmissions.
[bold]PRINT LOG[/bold] prints the full radio log. [bold]PRINT INTERCEPTS[/bold] prints only intercepted traffic.
Under [bold]TRAFFIC[/bold], each entry shows the transmission time, sender, and net, with the message itself on the line below.
## OPT - set configuration
OPT contains the radio's configurable operating settings.
Most lines cycle through their available options when you press ENT.
- [bold]MODE[/bold] - selects FREQ HOP, SINGLE CH, CIPHER, or PLAIN. See the waveform table on [textlink="the AN/PRC-117G" link="AU14CommsANPRC"]. - [bold]MONITOR[/bold] and [bold]SCAN[/bold] - the same functions available from the guided panel. - [bold]SQUELCH[/bold] - ranges from 0 to 4. Higher values remove more static and garbled traffic, but setting 4 may also suppress weak relay traffic. 3 is the standard setting. - [bold]OUTPUT[/bold] - selects LO, MED, or HI.
[bold]Power[/bold] [bold]Relay range[/bold] [bold]Battery[/bold] [bold]DF chance[/bold]
LO 60% Half Half
MED 100% Standard Standard
HI 150% Double Double
- [bold]BACKLIGHT[/bold] - night, day, or off. - [bold]TECHNIQUES[/bold] - opens BURST TX, POWER SAVE, PRIORITY WATCH, EMCON, and the STAKED SET controls. These are explained below. - [bold]STATION[/bold] - controls station identity and utility functions. - [bold]CALLSIGN[/bold] sets a fixed station callsign of up to 16 characters. Useful for command posts and staked sets. - [bold]CLEAR OVERRIDE[/bold] returns the radio to the current wearer's callsign. - [bold]ROSTER[/bold] selects from standard station names. - [bold]NET DIRECTORY[/bold], [bold]PHONE[/bold], and [bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] are also available here. - [bold]SET STATUS[/bold] - shows whether the radio is acting as a manpack or retrans station, the fitted antenna, which nets it is relaying, its coverage, and whether audio is going through the headset or handset. - [bold]LINK[/bold] - gives exact link information: - [bold]QUALITY[/bold] - link quality as a percentage. - [bold]VIA[/bold] - the relay carrying your signal, including its bearing and distance. - [bold]DRAW[/bold] - current battery drain per second. - [bold]ENDURANCE[/bold] - estimated minutes remaining at the current drain.
## Operator techniques
None of these are required for basic radio operation.
They are tools for situations where you deliberately want to trade range, convenience, battery life, or emissions for something else.
### Burst transmission
[bold]OPT > BURST TX[/bold]
Burst mode compresses each transmission before sending it.
It costs [bold]30% less battery[/bold] and has [bold]half the normal chance[/bold] of being direction-found. The message itself is unchanged.
Burst can be combined with LO output and SC or CT to greatly reduce the radio's detectable signature.
### Power save
[bold]OPT > POWER SAVE[/bold]
Power save lets the receiver sleep between messages, reducing idle battery drain by [bold]40%[/bold].
A sleeping receiver cannot watch every loaded net at once, so enabling power save disables [bold]SCAN[/bold] and [bold]PRIORITY WATCH[/bold].
Turning either SCAN or PRIORITY WATCH back on disables power save.
### Priority watch
[bold]OPT > PRIORITY WATCH[/bold]
Priority watch lets you monitor one of your other memories while continuing to work normally on the ON AIR memory.
For example, you can keep command traffic in your ear while transmitting on your squad net.
Unlike SCAN, priority watch does [bold]not[/bold] move your ON AIR memory around.
Your transmissions still go only through the working memory.
### EMCON
[bold]OPT > EMCON[/bold]
EMCON puts the radio into a listen-only emissions-control state.
While EMCON is active, the set performs [bold]no transmissions, no relay traffic, and no phone traffic[/bold]. There is therefore nothing for hostile direction-finding equipment to detect.
The radio still listens to and logs traffic on its working net.
Idle power draw also drops to one quarter of normal.
EMCON is useful when you need the set listening without broadcasting its position, or when conserving a battery over a long period.
[bold]Warning:[/bold] an AN/PRC in EMCON provides no relay coverage. Any nearby headset depending on that pack will lose its net.
### Staked set: retrans bridge
[bold]OPT > STAKED SET[/bold]
This option is available when the radio has been staked into the ground.
Select [bold]SIDE A[/bold] and [bold]SIDE B[/bold]. Each side must be one of the radio's memories containing a named net.
Then press ENT on [bold]BRIDGE[/bold].
Traffic received on either net is retransmitted onto the other under the radio's callsign, while preserving the original speaker in the message:
[bold][RXMT] SABRE 1-1: contact north[/bold]
A bridge can connect a squad net to command, or join two otherwise separate nets.
Every retransmission still counts as a transmission. It consumes battery and may be direction-found.
Retransmitted traffic is never retransmitted again, so two bridged radios cannot create an endless loop.
Packing the radio up immediately breaks the bridge.
### Staked set: peak the antenna
[bold]OPT > STAKED SET > PEAK THE ANTENNA[/bold]
Peaking takes about [bold]15 seconds[/bold]. Remain still while the antenna is being aimed and tuned.
Once complete, the staked radio's relay range increases by [bold]25%[/bold].
The bonus lasts until the radio is packed up.
### Over-the-air rekey
After a recrypto, every radio still holding one of your side's old cards has a superseded key and will transmit unsecured traffic.
Rather than replacing every card by hand, an expert operator carrying the [bold]current[/bold] key can distribute it over the air.
Use [bold]SEC > SEND KEY OTA[/bold].
The display tells you how many superseded sets are currently reachable.
Press ENT once to arm the push, then ENT again to send it.
- The new key reaches every friendly radio that is switched on, worn or staked, and within roughly 45 tiles. - It can also reach radios farther away if both you and the receiving set are connected through your side's command-net relay coverage. - Sending the key consumes a large amount of battery and may be direction-found. - The radio requires 30 seconds before another key push can be made.
[bold]There is a risk:[/bold] a captured radio that still contains one of your side's fill cards is still considered one of your sets.
If it is reachable, it receives the new key as well.
Destroy or invalidate captured fills before sending a new key whenever possible.
### Dwell
Dwell is used while the search receiver is running.
On the [bold]SRCH[/bold] page, place the cursor over a [bold]partial[/bold] contact and press ENT.
The search head stops sweeping and remains on that signal.
Every new transmission from the contact then counts [bold]double[/bold] toward resolving it. A busy net can therefore be identified in roughly half the normal time.
The trade-off is that the rest of the band goes completely unheard while you are dwelling.
Use [bold]RELEASE THE HEAD[/bold] to resume the normal sweep.
Once the contact fully resolves, the receiver resumes searching automatically.
### Jammer fix
The search receiver can also triangulate a jammer.
While a jammer is affecting your position, open [bold]SRCH > JAMMER DF[/bold].
1. Select [bold]TAKE A BEARING[/bold]. The radio records the exact compass bearing toward the jammer. 2. Move at least [bold]12 tiles[/bold]. The [bold]BASELINE[/bold] display tracks the distance for you. 3. Select [bold]TAKE SECOND BEARING[/bold].
The radio compares the two bearings and marks their intersection on your side's tactical map.
The jammer remains marked for [bold]two minutes[/bold], and the radio also reports its distance from you.
The first bearing expires after three minutes, so do not take too long establishing the second position.
## RETURN TO AUTO
Settings changed from the faceplate remain active when somebody switches back to the guided interface.
The guided panel shows those changes and provides [bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold] to restore its normal automatic configuration.
If you hand the radio to another operator while it is in EMCON, running a retrans bridge, or otherwise configured unusually, tell them first.
## Drill
If you want to learn the faceplate, run this once on a powered, worn radio with no nets loaded.
1. Press [bold]8[/bold] to open PGM. Select [bold]LOAD STD NETS[/bold] and press ENT. 2. Press [bold]7[/bold] for OPT. Move to [bold]OUTPUT[/bold] and press ENT until it reads [bold]LO[/bold]. Move to [bold]BURST TX[/bold] and enable it. 3. Move to [bold]PRIORITY WATCH[/bold] and select your command memory. 4. Press [bold]1[/bold] to send a radio check. Read the response in chat. 5. Return to OPT and open [bold]LINK[/bold]. Check which relay is carrying you and the radio's estimated endurance. 6. Switch back to the guided view. Open SETTINGS and confirm that your changes are listed there. Press [bold]RETURN TO AUTO[/bold].
The [bold]?[/bold] soft key opens the faceplate key card whenever you need a reminder.
